Government Offers Up to ₹25 Lakh Subsidized Loans for Poultry Farming Under NLM: Check Eligibility and Application Process

Government Announces Subsidized Loans for Poultry Farming Under National Livestock Mission

The Indian government has expanded access to subsidized loans for poultry farming under the National Livestock Mission (NLM), aiming to boost rural entrepreneurship and agricultural sector growth. Eligible individuals can receive up to 50% subsidy on project costs, with a maximum loan amount of ₹25 lakh, according to the official NLM portal.

Subsidy Structure and Loan Details

Under the NLM, applicants for poultry farming projects can avail of a capital subsidy covering 50% of the total project cost. For instance, if a farmer requires a ₹50 lakh loan to establish a poultry farm, the government will directly subsidize ₹25 lakh, reducing the repayment burden. The remaining 50% must be funded through bank loans or personal contributions. This initiative is part of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare’s broader strategy to promote sustainable livestock development.

Eligibility Criteria

To qualify for the subsidized loan, applicants must meet the following criteria:

  • Be an Indian citizen aged 18 years or above.
  • Operate as a self-employed individual or belong to registered entities such as Self-Help Groups (SHGs), Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Joint Livelihood Groups (JLGs), or companies registered under the Companies Act, 2013.
  • Propose a viable poultry farming project aligned with NLM guidelines.

Required Documents

Applicants must submit the following documents during the online application process:

  • Proof of identity (Aadhaar card, passport, etc.).
  • PAN card.
  • Business registration documents for poultry farming.
  • Land ownership or lease agreements for the project site.
  • Bank account details and statements.
  • Passport-size photographs.

Notably, the NLM does not require physical submission of documents; all paperwork is processed online via the official portal.

How to Apply

Interested candidates can apply for the subsidized loan through the NLM’s online portal at [www.nlm.udyamimitra.in](https://navbharattimes.indiatimes.com/personal-finance/loans/subsidy-of-up-to-rs-25-lakh-loan-for-poultry-farming-eligibility/articleshow/135251070.cms). The application process involves registering on the portal, filling out the project details, uploading required documents, and submitting the form. Post-submission, applicants must coordinate with their chosen bank to finalize the loan disbursement.

Broader Scope of NLM

While the focus here is on poultry farming, the NLM also supports loans for other livestock activities, including cattle, goat, and sheep rearing, as well as dairy production. The mission emphasizes areas like broiler farm establishment, hatchery development, and poultry back-end infrastructure.

Practical Implications and Verification

The subsidy significantly lowers the financial barrier for small-scale poultry entrepreneurs, particularly in rural areas. However, the exact interest rates, processing timelines, and repayment terms depend on individual banks and are not specified in the NLM guidelines. Prospective applicants should consult the official website or their selected financial institution for precise details.

To verify the information, readers are encouraged to visit the [NLM official portal](https://navbharattimes.indiatimes.com/personal-finance/loans/subsidy-of-up-to-rs-25-lakh-loan-for-poultry-farming-eligibility/articleshow/135251070.cms) or contact the Department of Animal Husbandry, Dairying and Fisheries (DAHD), Ministry of Agriculture. The online application system ensures a paperless process, but applicants should confirm document requirements with their bank before submission.

Conclusion

The NLM’s subsidized loan scheme represents a strategic move to empower rural entrepreneurs and enhance food security through poultry farming. With clear eligibility criteria and streamlined documentation, the initiative simplifies access to capital for sustainable agricultural ventures. As with any government program, applicants must adhere to procedural guidelines and seek official clarifications where necessary.
